newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai metal futures turnover falls in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai metal futures turnover falls in 1996.

text.p: Turnover of metals futures contracts on the Shanghai Metal Exchange dropped sharply to 230 billion yuan in 1996 from 455.84 billion yuan in 1995, Xinhua news agency reported on Friday.
Volume for 1996 fell to 11 million tonnes from 16.86 million tonnes in 1995, Xinhua said.
The exchange mainly trades copper and aluminium futures. Other contracts in lead, zinc, tin and nickel are rarely traded.
Shanghai traders said metals futures trading was hit by weakness on the world markets and domestic over-supply due to increased production and imports.

Despite the falls, trading in Shanghai rallied in the second half of 1996, with the turnover for the last six months up 58 percent over the first half, Xinhua quoted Zhou Xiaohong, a senior official of the Shanghai Metals Exchange, as saying.
Zhou was quoted as saying she expected more active trading in 1997.
